issues.title: Two section rhythms across the site from one section.section class
issues.note:
CLOSED 2026-08-04 — owner re-verified this one LIVE against the running build and confirmed the disposition. OWNER RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04 against the running build, and independently re-checked against dist. NOREPRO CONFIRMED, AND THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOW KNOWN — the owner is right that the ticket's framing is inaccurate, and the reason is more useful than the correction. THE SECTION PADDING TOKEN IS KEYED TO VIEWPORT HEIGHT, NOT WIDTH: --sec-pad-y is clamp(72px, 9.5vh, 144px). So 9.5vh at a 1000px-tall viewport is 95px, at 900px it is 85.5px, and the owner's 85.18px is that token at an iframe about 897px tall. EVERY ONE OF THESE FIGURES IS CORRECT AND ALL OF THEM DISAGREE, because "measured at 1440" says nothing about the padding. Two of my own runs disagreed with each other for exactly this reason — 900px high gave 85.5, 1000px high gave 95 — and the contradiction was chased as a caching or race problem before the token was read. AND THE "63px" GROUP IS A SECOND NAMED TOKEN, not the same class drifting: --sec-pad-y-sm is clamp(52px, 7vh, 100px), and 7vh at 900px is 63px exactly. It is used deliberately by Compare.astro, Glossary.astro, Sector.astro, compare/index, glossary/index and pricing.astro — precisely the routes the ticket listed as the 63px group. There is also --sec-pad-y-hero for the first block under the nav. CONFIRMING THE OWNER'S OTHER OBSERVATION: /compare, /glossary, /sectors, /blog and the four legal routes carry ZERO section.section elements — 25 of 43 routes do — so "one class producing two rhythms" is wrong twice over. Across all 43 dist routes at one fixed viewport there is exactly ONE pair, plus /faq's deliberate 0px top on its joined sections. THE RULE THIS LEAVES: a section-rhythm figure quoted without a viewport HEIGHT is unfalsifiable, and all three tokens should be quoted by name rather than by pixel.

issues.title: Trade mark exposure: Microsoft and Google marks used without the required permission
issues.note:
APPLIED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-04. color-microsoft-entra-id.svg (withdrawal 7) and color-google-drive.svg (withdrawal 8) are no longer referenced from src, and both were the vendor CORRECT CURRENT artwork -- which is why they survived withdrawals 1 to 6, and is the whole point: correct is not licensed. The files STAY ON DISK with WITHDRAWN rows in LOGO-PROVENANCE.md, which is the architecture rather than an oversight: check-vendor-logos.js rule 2 requires every recorded file to exist and rule 3 forbids a withdrawn row being served, so DELETING them would FAIL the build. VERIFIED: gate re-run reports 2 marks referenced (Confluence, Slack), 9 recorded, 7 withdrawn, exit 0; full 29-step build exit 0; and the BUILT OUTPUT now contains only color-confluence.svg and color-slack.svg with ZERO references to any Microsoft or Google file in any built HTML. No "Partner" language existed anywhere to remove, and the product names already ship as text so nothing a reader can use was lost. OPEN FOR THE OWNER, and it is the exposure A-57 turned out NOT to have: all five Microsoft/Google marks ARE already on origin/main and are publicly retrievable from the repo right now. Withdrawing them stops them SHIPPING; it does not unpublish them. Purging pushed history is a separate call and engages the standing no-rewrite rule. OWNER DECISION 2026-08-04. VERDICT: REMOVE both marks; do not seek licences. Strip the Microsoft and Google symbols entirely and replace with plain text ("Works with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace"), with NO "Partner" language. Rationale: near-zero conversion value from those logos, and CrowAgent is already on record in a UK IPO dispute — a second file of unlicensed third-party marks is the last thing that should be discoverable. Nominative text use is the low-risk form. ACTION: delete the three Microsoft marks and the Google G from the served assets and their call sites; replace with text; remove any "Partner" wording; KEEP LOGO-PROVENANCE.md as the audit record.

PRIOR RECORD — NOT an engineering call. Microsoft: a formal licence is generally required, the symbol and logotype must be used together (we use symbol only), and M365 app icons need a trademark licence. Three Microsoft marks are served and no licence is held. Entra ID is the correct current mark but comes from a pack whose terms exclude marketing use. Google: the G is for referring to Google the company, needs a co-branding arrangement for marketing, and must not sit on backgrounds that inhibit legibility, which our dark navy does. Recorded in LOGO-PROVENANCE.md, not silently fixed. Same class of risk as the Crowe trade mark remediation of July.

issues.title: Continuous execution loop running every 10 minutes
issues.note: RE-ARMED 2026-08-04 at the owner request ("start loop"). Self-paced rather than a fixed 10-minute cadence: the loop schedules its own next wake based on what it is waiting for, which avoids the quiet wake-ups the old fixed interval spent on a tree that had not changed. CONSTRAINTS UNCHANGED AND STILL BINDING: safe concurrency on this 15.7 GB machine is 2 to 3 agents; exceeding it has already emptied astro/dist once and taken every route to 404; verification is against BUILT OUTPUT, never an agent summary; and a second concurrent npm run build is the single biggest source of false readings. issues.title: Geometry measured below the fold reads the arrival animation, not the layout
issues.note: THE FALSIFICATION PASS PRODUCED FIVE FALSE FAILURES AND ALL OF THEM WERE THIS. The arrival animations on this site run on a SCROLL timeline — animation-timeline: view(). They are not one-shot: an element below the fold sits at its FROM keyframe, RETURNS there when you scroll away again, and reports playState "running" with currentTime NaN and duration auto the entire time. So every getBoundingClientRect() taken on an element outside its view range reads the PRE-ARRIVAL TRANSFORM RATHER THAN THE LAYOUT. On /about that fabricated a 30.8px offset between a heading and its artefact card — which is EXACTLY the defect O-46 had been reported as, so the harness appeared to have found a regression it had in fact invented. On /faq it fabricated a 27.2px seam between two groups by differencing two neighbouring sections at different points in their travel (translateY 0.33 against 27.5). A first attempt to explain that seam blamed a stray one-character text node in <main>; removing all seven such nodes in the live page moved the gap by 0.0px, which is why the cause was tested rather than asserted. THE RULE, and it applies to every future audit of this site: measure geometry EITHER under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, where tokens.css collapses the durations and the transforms resolve to none, OR via offsetTop/offsetHeight, which are layout and ignore transforms by definition. Scroll into view only when the question is genuinely about paint. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD IS LARGER THAN THIS ITEM: any earlier measurement on this site taken with getBoundingClientRect against an element below the first screen is suspect in the same way, including figures in AUDIT-2026-08-03.md. Re-measure before treating any of them as evidence. This is a sibling of the recorded hidden-tab trap, where a background tab froze transitions and produced false blank-section reports: both are cases of the measurement apparatus changing what it measures.

issues.title: A measurement harness that finds nothing must fail, not pass
issues.note: THREE separate false readings this session came from a harness measuring the wrong population rather than the wrong property, and each would have been reported as a site defect. (1) A-65 was checked on /glossary, which has ZERO <details> elements — "0 unmarked summaries" is a true sentence about a page with no summaries, and the honest form of the check is a sitewide crawl asserting it found at least 20. (2) A-74 reported .gl-back NOT FOUND because the probe built the URL "/glossary/ppn-002index.html" from a bad join; the element is present and measures exactly the 145.6x32 the note claimed. (3) The A-67 load sweep reported 44 of 44 routes 404 in every pass because `shell: true` on Windows split the document root at the space in "Crowagent Repo" and http-server was serving C:/Users/bhave/ Crowagent. THE GUARD THAT CATCHES ALL THREE is the same one: state the population the check requires and fail if it is absent, and preflight one known-good subject before believing any failure. The A-67 harness now refuses to report a site failure when its preflight route does not return 200 — which is how mistake (3) was caught rather than published.

issues.title: Section rhythm is keyed to viewport HEIGHT, so every "at 1440px" figure is under-specified
issues.note: THE SECOND MEASUREMENT TRAP FOUND THIS SESSION, and it invalidates a different class of figure from A-77. The three section-padding tokens are all keyed to vh: --sec-pad-y clamp(72px, 9.5vh, 144px), --sec-pad-y-sm clamp(52px, 7vh, 100px), --sec-pad-y-hero clamp(104px, 13vh, 188px). VIEWPORT WIDTH DOES NOT ENTER INTO IT — measured constant at 1100, 1200, 1280, 1290, 1366, 1400 and 1440. So a rhythm figure quoted as "85.5px at 1440" is unfalsifiable: 9.5vh is 95px at a 1000px-tall viewport, 85.5px at 900px, and 85.18px at the ~897px iframe the owner measured in. All three readings are correct and all three disagree. This produced a contradiction between two of my own runs in the same session, which was chased as a caching fault and a post-load race before the token was read — the source settled in one grep what four browser runs could not. IT ALSO EXPLAINS A-18 ENTIRELY: its "63px" group is 7vh at 900px, i.e. the separate and deliberate --sec-pad-y-sm, used by Compare, Glossary, Sector and pricing. THE RULE: quote the TOKEN, not the pixel, and state viewport height whenever a pixel is unavoidable. Sibling of A-77 (geometry below the fold reads the arrival animation) — both are cases where the measurement setup, not the site, decided the number.

issues.title: Terms still contracts for a free plan the site now says does not exist
issues.note: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING A-54, 2026-08-04, and it is the same defect one layer down where it is worse. A-54 deleted the published 14-day trial and /pricing now answers, in terms, that CrowMark is a paid product and THERE IS NO FREE PLAN. But src/content/legal/terms.md still contracts for one: line 27 states "Free plan usage is subject to monthly quota limits", and line 38 says the acceptable-use list "applies to all account types, free and paid". MARKETING COPY AND A CONTRACT DISAGREEING IS NOT THE SAME AS TWO PAGES DISAGREEING. Terms is the document a customer is bound by and the one that is read when there is a dispute, so the version that survives is the one saying a free plan exists. Either the free plan is real and /pricing is now wrong, or it is not and Terms describes an account type the product does not offer. NOT EDITED, deliberately: which of those is true is a commercial fact the repository cannot settle, and rewriting a clause in Terms to match a marketing decision is exactly the move that needs a person. VERIFIED, not taken on report: both lines read directly from the file. Also verified in the same pass that terms.md and security.md contain NO trial promise at all — the three grep hits that looked like one are a 14-day appeals window, a 14-day notice period for Terms changes, and a 14-day patch SLA for High-severity vulnerabilities. The earlier concern that A-54 would require editing contractual language was wrong, and this is the real issue that was hiding behind it.

'As per architecture and design' means genuine BEST PRACTICE, not whatever we previously recorded as agreed. A prior decision is evidence, not authority.
One semantic per hue, and violet is spoken for: violet means the engine REFUSED something. No other role may enter that hue family.
No justification-by-assertion in code comments or data files. A file may not state a reason that is not true of the tree.
No conceded field returns without Aparajita signing it off in writing.
Centre up to 3 lines; left-align beyond. A line count is a rendered fact, so the gate for it must measure the painted page.
